title: Locked dual-wield Drive crash: native loading contract and read-only weapon plan
status: Helper frozen for independent review and root integration; no live test
scope: User reports Final Form crash during transformation with empty secondary weapon; native static analysis and isolated helper implementation only.

claims.Finding: Fresh character-save initialization creates ten 56-byte form records with weapon WORD+0=0, level BYTE+2=1, byte+3=1, EXP0 and zero abilities. A locked form normally has a valid initial level but no secondary weapon.
claims.Limitations: Does not establish the contents of the user's current save.

claims.Finding: Normal acquisition of a type21 form item resolves the form command and assigns a weapon for forms1,4,5 when their weapon slot is empty. It scans owned type2 items, removes one from inventory and stores its ID; it also handles form acquisition and Anti EXP state.
claims.Limitations: The full function has inventory and unlock side effects and is not an appropriate silent repair call.

claims.Finding: The target form model is WORD form-table[form+11]; base Sora uses the current world costume mapping.
claims.Limitations: A model-table entry alone does not guarantee all dependent assets are present.

claims.Finding: For weapon slot1 of character ID1 or14, selects the form record by signed BYTE object+87 and reads its leading weapon WORD. A zero weapon returns zero before model mapping; a nonzero weapon uses WORD object+78 as its mapping group.
claims.Limitations: The optional constructor branch is not a guarantee that a dual-wield form can later operate without its weapon.

claims.Finding: Maps the item to a weapon object using went[group] plus WORD item-row+4, with the addition and multiplication in 64-bit address arithmetic. Zero group/item/base returns zero; a missing item row is dereferenced without a native null guard.
claims.Limitations: Native code supplies no payload-size check. Item type is validated by the helper before this mapping is mirrored.

claims.Finding: Selects a 32-byte name at wmst+32*(slot+2*group). Empty first byte returns no MSET; otherwise formats obj/<name>.mset.
claims.Limitations: A bounded nonempty filename does not prove that a modded package actually contains the file or that its contents are valid.

claims.Finding: Recursively requests each nonzero weapon model and its MSET. A zero result from3E0CC0 skips both requests for that hand.
claims.Limitations: The subsequent asynchronous loader and dependent file integrity remain engine responsibilities.

claims.Finding: Sora construction creates the second weapon only if form is1..6 or10 and3E0CC0(object,1) returns a nonzero object ID. With a zero form weapon, no second weapon actor is allocated.
claims.Limitations: This shows a missing actor, not the precise faulting instruction in the user's crash.

claims.Finding: Allocates and constructs a3088-byte weapon actor, stores it in parent+3424+8*slot, then configures its motion. Slot1 is therefore parent+3432.
claims.Limitations: Allocation failure also has unguarded follow-up calls; that general out-of-memory case is distinct from the reported locked-form problem.

claims.Finding: The weapon constructor uses the same wmst slot name; an empty MSET row skips loading, parent motion linkage and attachment. A usable offhand therefore requires a mapping result and a nonempty bounded motion name.
claims.Limitations: The constructor also relies on valid loaded model/bone/motion resources; this helper does not validate all binary asset contents.

claims.Finding: Bone selectors0x4004/0x4006/0x4008 can select the second weapon through3B5450(index1), then3D7600 and3B5D40 consume the weapon without a matching absent-offhand guard.
claims.Limitations: Independent agent evidence. Combined with the missing actor this is a concrete null-consumer path; no crash dump or live fault address was captured.

claims.Finding: Publishes the loaded system BAR at2AE5E50. First type2/tag went and wmst entries are decoded and installed as globals2AE5A38 and2AE5A40.
claims.Limitations: Unusual loaders that replace these globals independently of the owning BAR are conservatively unsupported by the repair helper.

claims.Finding: The allocation immediately preceding the loaded BAR has DWORD size at-16, magic0x23234141 at-12 and kind1 at-8. Size is rounded up to64 bytes before allocation.
claims.Limitations: The outer bound includes up to63 bytes of allocation padding. Per-entry size supplies the tighter payload bound.

claims.Finding: BAR lookup uses signed count at+4 and16-byte entries starting+16, matching type WORD+0 and tag DWORD+4. It returns the first matching occurrence without filtering the link flag.
claims.Limitations: Helper preserves first-match behavior and rejects malformed first matches rather than accepting later duplicates.

claims.Finding: BAR fixup publishes the encoded container self pointer at header+8 and replaces nonempty entry offsets at entry+8 with encoded pointers, preserving entry+12 lengths.
claims.Limitations: Helper requires a fixed loaded BAR, not an untouched on-disk BAR image.

claims.Finding: The developer system-table conversion path passes went entry DWORD+12 as the payload size to3EFE50, independently confirming the size field used to bound the mapping table.
claims.Limitations: This exporter is evidence only; the helper neither calls it nor mutates the BAR.

contract.api: bool PlanFormWeapon(unsigned form,const progression::ItemTable& items,uint16_t& replacement)
contract.reads: No game writes and no engine calls. Caller supplies stable scene/game-thread/save/item-table gates.
contract.forms: 0/2/3/6 return true with replacement0. Forms1/4/5 require a usable offhand. Invalid form>6 rejects.
contract.preserve: If existing form slot is a resolvable type2 Keyblade with valid model mapping and MSET name, replacement remains0.
contract.repair: Otherwise use current Sora primary weapon WORD9ABDA0, only if it passes the same target-form-specific mapping/model/MSET checks. No item grant, inventory removal or unlock check.
contract.bounds: Bind went/wmst globals to first matching system-BAR entries and bound all reads by allocation size and per-entry payload size. Validate overflow before address arithmetic; decode packed pointers using the bridge helper.
contract.integration: Plan during request preflight and again immediately before the native transition. Commit only the planned form-slot WORD before the asynchronous loader starts; the root module owns mutation, persistence and rejected-start handling.
contract.persistence: A committed usable weapon must remain available for the native transition and later status rebuilds. Root integration documents this as a save-progression change; the helper itself implements no undo.

limitations: No live reproduction or exception dump; native evidence supports the reported failure mechanism rather than identifying the user's exact fault RIP.
Named model/MSET entries do not prove files are present or well-formed in arbitrary mod packages.
Outer allocation metadata and BAR descriptors are assumed to belong to the supported native resource loader; replacement loader layouts reject.
No whole-function form-acquisition call is made because its inventory consumption and unlock side effects exceed this repair.
The untouched Gummi v0.8 work remains paused and unintegrated.
